title: Olin Declares $0.20 Quarterly Dividend, Its 400th in a Row
summary: Olin Corporation declared a $0.20 quarterly dividend, payable December 11, 2026, marking 100 years of consecutive quarterly dividend payments.
body_markdown:
According to the company, this dividend marks 100 years of consecutive quarterly dividend payments to its shareholders and is its 400th consecutive quarterly dividend. "Olin's century-long record of consecutive quarterly dividend payments reflects the enduring strength and resilience of our company, spanning diverse economic cycles, evolving markets, and significant corporate transformations," said Ken Lane, President and Chief Executive Officer.


## Why It Matters for OLN


The company presents the declaration as a centennial milestone. Lane said reaching it "is a meaningful reminder of Olin's long history of delivering value to shareholders," adding that Olin remains "focused on disciplined capital allocation, strengthening our business, and positioning Olin to create value for generations to come."


The release also states that the payment of cash dividends is subject to the discretion of Olin's Board of Directors, which may change the dividend policy, including the frequency or amount of any dividend, in light of then-existing conditions. It does not say how the $0.20 amount compares with the prior quarterly payment. Its forward-looking statements also refer to Olin's proposed merger with Huntsman, whose completion the company says depends on conditions including required regulatory approvals.
